name: strypt v0.3.0
body:
Built from `12c61fb54481022ae634f7c68ee9a361e2c01e3b` by `scripts/build-release.sh`; each binary was built twice, byte-identical.
The GUI's `.app` and AppImages were packaged twice, byte-identical; the `.dmg` around the `.app` is not reproducible.
Each file has a CycloneDX SBOM, `<file>.cdx.json`, listed in `SHA256SUMS`.

```sh
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing
gh attestation verify <file> -R FadeHack/strypt
```

name: strypt v0.1.2
body:
**A PDF whose page tree names one object more than once is now refused.** Rewriting such a file
dropped an object, and in the file that found this it was the document's only page, reported as a
success. Every release up to and including 0.1.1 is affected. Nothing leaked and no output was
wrong, so this is not a security fix; the risk is a saved copy missing a page. Found by the pdf
fuzz target ([ADR-0057](https://github.com/FadeHack/strypt/blob/v0.1.2/docs/DECISIONS.md),
[CHANGELOG](https://github.com/FadeHack/strypt/blob/v0.1.2/CHANGELOG.md)).

---

name: strypt v0.1.1
body:
> **Security fix.** 0.1.0 left the Exif (GPS, camera serial, author) of JPEG photos inside a PDF, and of its page thumbnails, while reporting the file clean. If you published a PDF cleaned by 0.1.0, check it with `exiftool -ee`. Details: [GHSA-fxhm-mvqq-vhhx](https://github.com/FadeHack/strypt/security/advisories/GHSA-fxhm-mvqq-vhhx) and [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/FadeHack/strypt/blob/v0.1.1/CHANGELOG.md).
